title: Reinvent the Operation not the Architecture: Quantum-inspired High-order Product for Compatible and Improved LLMs Training

problem.claim: The work addresses the basic inner-product and matrix-multiplication operations used in neural networks.

gap.claim: Innovation in network operations is presented as a direction orthogonal to work on new architectures, position encodings, and training algorithms.

contributions.claim: A quantum-inspired high-order tensor-product operation is proposed using high-dimensional Hilbert space.
The method re-parameterizes low-order vectors and matrices into an expressive high-order form without extra model parameters and with negligible reported computational overhead.
C2Q-SFT is proposed as a classic-to-quantum protocol that continues supervised fine-tuning by transparently replacing standard operations.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The operation is reported to apply in Transformers to token embeddings, attention query/key/value components, and the MLP.
Experiments are reported to show advantages for training from scratch and downstream-task fine-tuning across LLM scales.
C2Q-SFT is reported to consistently outperform standard SFT, with relative improvements of 0.56% on MMLU and 0.61% on GSM8k.

narrative_sequence.summary: The work reconsiders basic neural-network operations.
It proposes a quantum-inspired high-order tensor product and re-parameterization with no extra parameters and about 2% overhead.
The operation is applied to key Transformer components and used in the C2Q-SFT protocol.
The authors report benefits across training settings and relative improvements on MMLU and GSM8k.
The approach positions operation-level innovation as complementary to architecture, position-encoding, and training-algorithm changes.

source_observation.claim: A transparent replacement of basic operations is reported to work across token embeddings, attention components, and the MLP.

interpretation.claim: Operation-level interventions may provide a broad compatibility path across multiple model components.

application.claim: When improving an existing model, evaluate operation substitutions that preserve the surrounding architecture and training interface.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify which architectural, scale, or task conditions limit this compatibility.

source_observation.claim: The reported relative improvements are 0.56% on MMLU and 0.61% on GSM8k, with about 2% computational overhead.

interpretation.claim: Small reported gains may be presented as worthwhile when the added computational cost is also small.

application.claim: Compare operation-level methods using both task gains and incremental compute rather than either metric alone.

exception.claim: The abstract does not provide variance, baselines beyond standard SFT, or details of the computational measurement.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the high-order tensor-product formulation.
The abstract does not describe datasets, model scales, training settings, or experimental protocols.
The abstract does not report statistical variation or independent verification.
